## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Pānadhidāyakattheraapadāna* is a Pali verse text included within the *Therāpadāna* section of the Khuddaka Nikāya. Modern translations of the text are cataloged in five languages.

Automated analysis by DharmaNexus records extensive text reuse across the Pali canon and post-canonical literature, identifying 288 shared matches across 77 Pali works [DharmaNexus]. Substantial portions of the poem (§0.3–17.1) appear closely shared with the commentary on the *Theragāthā* (*Theragāthā-aṭṭhakathā*, Paṭhamo bhāgo), with additional parallels in its second volume [DharmaNexus]. In addition, formulaic verses (particularly in segments 16–21) are shared with many other *Therāpadāna* texts, including the *Sabbadāyakattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 401), the *Ekāsanadāyakattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 425), the *Madhudāyakattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 396), the *Mahākoṭṭhikattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 539), and the *Mañcadāyakattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 422) [DharmaNexus]. DharmaNexus also detects minor cross-language alignments with the Tibetan *Ārya-mañjuśrīmūlatantra* (D0543), though these exhibit low algorithmic plausibility scores and do not represent verified historical parallels [DharmaNexus].

*No discussion of this text was found in the reference-literature corpus; the overview relies on catalog and DharmaNexus data.*
